notes.title: Information on Accessibility
notes.notes: [p]These are for the time being our information on accessibility. Our game is pretty accessible and still in development. Many features are only planned as of now. Information are categorized by different kinds of disabilities. Known barriers are grouped at the beginning and will be repeated below.[/p][h2]Known Barriers[/h2][list][*][p]This game contains sensitive content that may be re-traumatizing, especially for people that survived social or sexual trauma.[/p][/*][*][p]The game does not support sign language.[/p][/*][*][p]The game is not available with simple or easy English.[/p][/*][*][p]The game has many emotional stories. Much is written in between lines. It is a game to think about. That is difficult.[/p][/*][*][p]Listening to the stories takes a lot of concentration.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Accessibility Features[/h2][h3]Post Traumatic Disorders[/h3][list][*][p]This game uses content notes to inform about sensitive topics.[/p][list][*][p]Content Notes are integrated into the play experience[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][i]planned: Sequences can be skipped.[/i][/p][list][*][p][i]planned: there will be neutral summaries for sequences.[/i][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]Motor Impairments[/h3][list][*][p][i]planned: Controls can be customized using SteamInput.[/i][/p][/*][*][p]There are no quick-time-events or sequences that require high input skills.[/p][/*][*][p]The game can be controlled in multiple modes:[/p][list][*][p]Mouse and Keyboard (classic FPS)[/p][/*][*][p]Gamepad (classic FPS)[/p][/*][*][p][i]planned:  only mouse or only touchpad (point-and-click-style controls)[/i][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]Visual Impairments[/h3][list][*][p]The game can be understood playing color-blind. A color correction filter is not provided. This is because many find them mostly unhelpful.[/p][/*][*][p]All Interfaces have sufficient contrast. (At least 7:1 for normal text and 4.5:1 for big text)[/p][/*][*][p]The UI can be scaled.[/p][/*][*][p][i]planned: Text can be displayed with a hyper-legible font[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]planned: Text can be displayed using the default font of your operating System.[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]planned: Text can be read by a screen-reader.[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]planned: The game can be played fully blind. It can be navigated like a website[/i][/p][/*][/list][h3]Hearing Impairments[/h3][list][*][p]The game can be played fully deaf.[/p][/*][*][p][i]planned: the game has closed captioning.[/i][/p][/*][*][p]The game does [b]not[/b] support sign language.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Cognitive Impairments[/h3][list][*][p]The game is not available with simple or easy English.[/p][/*][*][p]There are no decisions that need to be taken under time pressure.[/p][/*][*][p]The game has many emotional stories. Much is written in-between lines. It is a game to think about. That is difficult.[/p][/*][/list][h3]ADHD[/h3][list][*][p]The game requires a lot of listening and concentration.[/p][/*][*][p][i]planned: the game will have a built-in fidget toy in each bunk-bed.[/i][/p][/*][/list][p]Side-node: [i]Yeah it is pretty ironic that a game on ADHD is not really ADHD accessible. We've realized that pretty late in development, but in my defense: I have ADHD.[/i][/p][h3]Miscellaneous[/h3][list][*][p]Text, Music and Speech volume can be configured.[/p][/*][*][p]The game has a mode with reduced motion. It recognizes the reduce motion setting on apple devices.[/p][/*][*][p]There is a filter that muffles high frequencies and tones down overwhelming noises,[/p][/*][*][p]The game is Open Source. It is easy to develop your own accessibility-mods.[/p][/*][*][p]The game can always be saved and loaded.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Raising Issues and Filing Complaints[/h2][p]If you find an issue, let us know via [url="mailto:support@polynormal.games"]support@polynormal.games[/url].[/p][p]These information are voluntary. As a small business, we are exempt from German regulation of barrier-free access to digital services. If Germany followed its laws, you could file a formal complaint with a supervising agency if we ignored your complaints.[/p][p]This agency does not exist for the jurisdiction of Saxony as of now.[/p][p]If you want to file a complaint about not being able to file a complaint, we presume that the State [url="https://www.sk.sachsen.de/en/state-commissioner-for-the-inclusion-of-persons-with-disabilities-5363.html"]Commissioner for the Inclusion of Saxony[/url] has jurisdiction.[/p]

notes.title: FINAL development livestream!
notes.notes: [p]To celebrate the end of next fest, we will be holding yet another development live stream here on Steam.[/p][p]Today we're not going to let ourselves get distracted by bugfixing and actually get to work on creating stunning shaders for our subway![/p][p]So join us to take a look at what is possible with the power of Godot and Open Source. Make sure to also ask any questions you may have in the live chat. If I'm not too distracted by, I may even get to answering them.[/p][p]But don't stress yourself too much: You will still be able to play our demo after this next fest and there will very likely even more development insights before our release.[/p]

notes.title: VFX magic and live game development
notes.notes: [p]Do you want to see the magic sauce that is making this game feel so alive? Well today you can join us while we create some awesome shaders so our subway train-car trough time can spring to life![/p][p]We will be showing you how to do shaders and texture baking in blender, but we will also show you the dark magic that is shaders in Godot. prepare for minds to be blown and trains to be dipped into a river of time.[/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/WjduEh4htP"]Join our discord[/url] if you want to test the demo live and have the develpers participate in you finding your next favorite game.[/p][p]Thanks to [url="https://www.twitch.tv/zharwyn"]Zharwyn[/url] for playing our game and letting us live-react to the gameplay![/p]

notes.title: Hello World, this is my Cyber Deck!
notes.notes:
Last Spring, I was very excited as I finally got my SteamDeck in the mail. The big day came aaaand ... my Laptop died.

This is how the Steam Deck unironically became my main mobile workstation for about a year, and while I admittedly would not go back to it, it was a lot more usable than you might suspect.

This is why i am also proud to announce: My Game will have FULL Steam Deck Support.

As of now, without much optimization, the game is already running well above the 40FPS target for running games smoothly at the lower display refresh rate and I am pretty sure I will be able to hit the 60FPS mark, hopefully even without any 3D render scaling. But as this is a cozy walking sim, you will likely not notice small stutters anyway.

The game furthermore has full controller support and plays a lot better on the Steam Deck, as especially the touch screen will get a lot of utilization.

Font rendering is being considered, as my game has a lot of text and I put a lot of emphasis on accessibility. This is an area that right now needs more development.

I will also look into using the joypads and the accelerator for input, but do not want to promise anything right now.
